root.label: Conversion functions and explicit
root.note: User-defined conversions in both directions, at most one per implicit conversion.

children.label: Two directions
children.note: A constructor converts into the class; operator U() converts out of it.

children.label: Converting constructor
children.note: Any non-explicit constructor, including multi-parameter ones used by braced lists.

children.label: Conversion function
children.note: No parameters, no declared return type; may be const, virtual, a template or operator auto.

children.label: Never used implicitly
children.note: Conversion to the class itself, a base class, or void is never applied implicitly.

children.label: One-conversion limit
children.note: At most one user-defined conversion is applied implicitly to a single value.

children.label: Standard conversions around
children.note: Promotions or conversions may come before and after the one user-defined call.

children.label: Two hops fail
children.note: const char* to std::string to Name is two user-defined conversions, so it fails.

children.label: Per value
children.note: Direct-initialization converts a constructor's argument separately, so B b(1) can work where B b = 1 fails.

children.label: Candidate sets
children.note: The form of initialization decides which functions are even considered.

children.label: Copy-initialization
children.note: Converting constructors plus non-explicit conversion functions; explicit ones are not candidates.

children.label: Direct-initialization
children.note: All constructors, plus explicit conversion functions followed by at most a qualification conversion.

children.label: Copy-list-initialization
children.note: Explicit constructors are candidates, and choosing one makes it ill-formed.

children.label: Ctor versus conv function
children.note: A(const B&) and B::operator A() const make A a = B{} ambiguous.

children.label: explicit operator bool
children.note: C++11 replacement for the safe-bool idiom.

children.label: Contextual contexts
children.note: if, while, for, do, !, &&, ||, the first operand of ?:, static_assert and noexcept(expr).

children.label: Not contextual
children.note: bool b = f, return f, f == true and int i(f) are all ill-formed.

children.label: Safe-bool history
children.note: Before C++11, classes converted to a member pointer so they were testable but not arithmetic.

children.label: explicit(bool)
children.note: C++20: a constant bool decides whether the constructor is explicit.

children.label: Conditionally explicit
children.note: explicit(!is_convertible_v<U, T>) makes a wrapper exactly as implicit as T.

children.label: Library use
children.note: std::pair and std::optional constructors are conditionally explicit this way.

children.label: Conversion templates
children.note: template<class T> operator T() deduces T from the required target type.

children.label: Deduction rule
children.note: References and top-level cv are stripped, so const int& deduces int.

children.label: Converts to anything
children.note: Makes every overload viable; constrain it to avoid accidental matches.
